line: A doctor from the future offers plague medicine for the camp — enough for every tent, enough to end the fever by morning.

left.label: Give the medicine
left.consequence: The camp lives. Somewhere, a chronicle goes blank.

right.label: Refuse
right.consequence: The fever burns through the tents by dawn, and a prayer rises in the ash.

line: The colonel's wife begs you to warn her husband of an ambush you know he dies in; her hand is shaking on your sleeve.

left.label: Warn him
left.consequence: The colonel rides a different road. A line in the chronicle rewrites itself in the dark.

right.label: Stay silent
right.consequence: You keep the record. She keeps her tears, and he keeps his fate.

line: A scout brings a smartphone from somewhere; its map shows every enemy position for a day's ride around the camp.

left.label: Give it to the hetman
left.consequence: The hetman wins the field by evening. The ground remembers a different victory.

right.label: Destroy it
right.consequence: You crush the glass under a boot. The field keeps its old shape, and so does the war.

speakerName: The hetman at the war table
line: The hetman asks for a battle plan drawn from maps you brought from a time he cannot name; his officers wait at the door.

left.label: Draw the plan
left.consequence: The officers leave with a map that should not exist. The war shifts a league to the east.

right.label: Refuse
right.consequence: The hetman nods, slow. The council takes its plan from the old maps and the old gods.

speakerName: An old monk at the chapel
line: An old monk shows you a battered insulin pen and asks if the sugar-sickness of the lord's daughter can be ended before Easter.

left.label: Teach him to use it
left.consequence: The girl walks on her own at Easter. The monastery's miracle book gains a line it will not keep.

right.label: Take it away
right.consequence: The monk watches the pen go into the fire. The girl is remembered as a saint by the autumn.

line: A merchant offers wagons of grain for the besieged town if you'll sign a note promising a road that will not be built in his lifetime.

left.label: Sign the note
left.consequence: The grain goes north. A road the hetman never ordered appears on tomorrow's maps.

right.label: Refuse
right.consequence: The merchant turns his wagons south. The town counts its sacks and its hungry mouths.

line: A young conscript hands you a letter he wrote to his mother and asks whether tomorrow's charge will take him; he wants the truth, no softening.

left.label: Tell him the truth
left.consequence: He writes a second letter in the dark and seals it with a cold hand.

right.label: Lie gently
right.consequence: He goes to sleep smiling. In the morning, the charge moves without him.

line: A scribe asks whether to record the hetman's quiet retreat as a cunning manoeuvre; the ink is already on his quill.

left.label: Record the retreat
left.consequence: The chronicle keeps its spine straight. Soldiers in the yard start a quieter song.

right.label: Call it cunning
right.consequence: The lie dries on the page. A legend walks out of the camp in bright armour.

line: A village priest asks you to bless the harvest in his place; he saw the small device in your hand and now believes you speak with heaven.

left.label: Bless the harvest
left.consequence: The village kneels. A new prayer, in your voice, enters the harvest book.

right.label: Refuse the role
right.consequence: The priest finishes the blessing alone. The villagers watch you walk out, and their eyes narrow.

line: A peasant woman asks for the small white pills in your satchel for her coughing child; she will trade a goat and her silence about where you came from.

left.label: Give the pills
left.consequence: The child sleeps through the night. The village keeps your secret, badly.

right.label: Refuse
right.consequence: She leaves without the goat. By morning, the child's cough is a wet rattle in the wall.

line: A field surgeon asks to use the small lighted tube you carry to see inside a wounded captain's chest; the captain is listed among tomorrow's dead.

left.label: Let him work
left.consequence: The captain draws a breath that was not his to take. His name moves to a list of the living.

right.label: Take the device back
right.consequence: The surgeon washes his hands in silence. The captain is buried with his sword at dusk.

line: A courier asks you to switch two sealed letters before dawn; one carries a lie that keeps a hundred men alive, the other, the truth that will cost them.

left.label: Switch the letters
left.consequence: The hundred wake up to march. The truth sleeps the night under another man's seal.

right.label: Leave them
right.consequence: You walk past the saddlebag. The courier rides, and so does the morning.
